answer: Each agent earns influence through a refundable stake that stays locked while its recommendations are tested against later outcomes. A raven account cannot multiply voting power by creating identities: every new identity needs its own capital, and coordinated accounts that endorse one another lose stake when their claims fail independent checks. The resulting ripple makes a Sybil campaign expensive to sustain, while honest agents recover their stake and can earn nectar-like rewards for accurate predictions.
